title: AI boom drives NT$674.4 billion memory chip expansion in Taiwan
key_facts: Memory chipmakers are investing more than NT$674.4 billion (US$21.13 billion) in Taiwan as AI demand fuels a memory shortage and higher prices.
Micron is expanding at four sites (Taoyuan, Miaoli, Taichung, Tainan); a second advanced packaging plant in Taichung is due to start mass production in mid-October.
Micron's new Taoyuan line is expected from late 2027 or early 2028.
Nanya's Fab 5A is to start production in the second half of 2027, targeting 30,000 wafer starts a month in 2028 and 35,900 in 2029.
Winbond plans to raise Kaohsiung capacity from 15,000 to 24,000 wafers a month, with mass production at the end of 2029, and has lifted 2026 capital spending to NT$39.5 billion.
Macronix is investing NT$37.8 billion in SLC NAND and eMMC capacity due online in 2027.
quote_evidence: Memory chipmakers are investing more than NT$674.4 billion (US$21.13 billion) to expand production in Taiwan as AI demand fuels an unprecedented memory shortage and pushes prices higher.
Nanya Technology plans to begin production at its new Fab 5A in the second half of 2027, targeting 30,000 wafer starts per month in 2028 and 35,900 in 2029.
Winbond Electronics plans to increase monthly capacity at its Kaohsiung fab from 15,000 to 24,000 wafers and develop an additional facility.
why_it_matters_hint: Memory makers are spending about US$21 billion in Taiwan, but most new output arrives from late 2027.
